# Unit3 practical evidence activities
Original teacher-led clinic,14October2026. Embed in existing weeks2,7–9,12–15 practice slots; replace equivalent exercises, no new weeks/project. Record actual learner evidence, do not prefill results.

E1 — Independent algorithms (P05/P19): use pseudocode clinic. Create a fresh 2D traversal, dictionary operation and search/sort algorithm. State contracts, predict results, translate/check in Python, and annotate assignment/comparison/bounds. Teacher checks clarity and source conventions.
E2 — Debugger (P24): use existing isolated return fault. Predict active/availability/quantity before the second return. Set a breakpoint immediately before the stock update, capture watched state, step, identify the missing guard and repair it. Record focused retest and regression evidence. If no debugger is available, print/trace evidence can support isolation, but mark breakpoint demonstration pending.
E3 — Representative environment (P21): use existing reliability_load.py with100/1000records and optional CSV on a teacher-controlled machine. Record machine/Python/source version, input volume/bytes, transaction mix, repeats, expected/actual counts and times. Agree criteria first. Synthetic offline measurements are not deployment/concurrency proof. Use teacher-approved representative data/workflows with no sensitive information; retain unresolved differences from target environment.
E4 — Address-plan application (N10): new parent192.168.120.0/24; Studio30endpoints+gateway, Staff12+gateway, Devices5+gateway, Guests4+gateway. Allocate smallest ordinaryLANblocks, aligned/nonoverlapping, gateways and reserve. Apply in an isolated simulator or assigned lab, using teacher-specified addressing; paper design alone leaves application pending. Do not apply fictional addresses to the school network.
E5 — Network conventions (N15): consult SCSA support booklet printedp12 and official Cisco icon reference. Identify cloud/router/modem/switch/AP/end-device/file-server/database-server/firewall symbols; draw a legend with labels. Redraw a perimeter diagram: WAN -> service termination -> firewall -> trusted routed network -> access switches/AP/end devices. For the course convention, perimeter firewall sits outside the trusted network and needs no IP label; put gateways on the router. Show four subnets, physical link/media/rates, representative endpoints and policy location. Real appliances may combine routing/firewall functions: distinguish that from the simplified course diagram. Internal restrictions still need relevant inter-zone filtering, not just perimeter placement.
E6 — Live tools (N14): teacher provides exact authorised responding target and context. Record host/prefix/gateway without changing them; run a small ping sample and traceroute to that target. Windows: ping -n4 TARGET (write as ping -n 4 TARGET), tracert -d TARGET. Save output with timestamp/load. Interpret sent/received/RTTs, missing replies and possible filtering. Check a required service separately. Synthetic logs may rehearse interpretation but do not demonstrate actual execution. No scans or unassigned targets are needed.

Submit evidence CSV plus selected code/trace/diagram/log references. Use synthetic learner IDs locally; do not upload student names/results to the site. Teacher signs off observation only after checking. Activities are teaching/evidence collection, not an official assessment or blanket completion claim.
